To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a high‐resolution genetic map of soybean using next‐generation sequencing and identified QTL regions that are associated with seed composition traits.
the bin map derived by whole‐genome re‐sequencing technology enhanced the mapping resolution (from Mb to Kb) and identified novel QTLs for protein, oil and sucrose content.
we identified novel and major QTLS for protein, oil and sucrose content that can be exploited for soybean improvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the genomic hotspots underlying variation in protein, oil, sucrose, and other agronomic traits in soybean.
the identification of genomic loci that could be utilized for marker‐assisted selection (MAS) and genomic selection (GS) in soybean.
dissecting the genomic hotspots underlying protein, oil, sucrose content, and domestication in cultivated soybean using an interspecific RIL population derived from G. max and G. soija.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study provides a comprehensive and detailed analysis of genomic hotspots underlying protein, oil, sucrose content, and their relationship in an interspecific population of soybean.
the bin map developed in this study provides a valuable resource for fine‐mapping of genomic loci and QTLs for agronomically important traits in cultivated soybean.
genomic loci underlying protein, oil, sucrose, and domestication‐related genes were identified and validated in the present study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

high‐resolution bin mapping derived from next‐gen sequencing technology can be used to identify genomic hotspots for important seed quality traits in soybean and that wild soybean could be used as an important genetic resource for cultivated soybean.
we developed a high‐resolution genetic map and dissected the genetic architecture of seed composition traits in soybean.
the combination of bin mapping, 3K‐QTL analysis, and GWAS identified the genomic hotspots for protein, oil and sucrose content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high‐density bin map derived from whole‐genome sequencing technology can enhance the precision of QTL analysis and can be utilized to identify novel candidate genes.
the bin map derived using next‐generation sequencing data provides an opportunity for fine‐scale genetic mapping and identification of genomic hotspots underlying important agronomic traits.
the high‐resolution bin mapping using next‐generation sequencing data provides a valuable resource for soybean genetic improvement and breeding.
